utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, Admiral, of the affirmation you took at the commencement, which still applies. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Admiral Jokic. I would ask you, please, to turn your attention to tab 22. Admiral, you have in front of you a document dated 24 October, 1991. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document produced by my command, and it bears my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, I want to ask you to comment on some provisions of the document. First of all, to whom is the document addressed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is addressed to all the subordinate units of my command. It was produced based on the report of the superior command, the 2nd Operational Group, indicating that during the operations conducted by the Trebinje Brigade, five soldiers have been killed and eight wounded. And that due to that, certain measures were to be taken to avoid this situation arising again. This is a report and it is a request to take certain measures with respect to improvements to control and command with respect to reconnaissance, other operations, discipline, firing, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was your view that the number of casualties was excessive under circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was your view that lack of discipline or willfulness may have been involved in the combat activities that you are addressing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And was there a concern on your part about use --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Let me finish my question to you, Admiral, and then you can respond. Were you concerned about the overall skill or lack thereof with which the operation had been carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, there were errors that were made by lower-ranking commands subordinate to the command; these were battalion and company commanders that made these errors. These were professional issues. It was about applying certain rules of combat when in combat, especially as concerned those officers that were supposed to apply those rules. The superior command noticed these shortcomings and these unacceptable losses, and then an order was issued to those commands to eliminate them. I was concerned by the fact that this brigade was supposed to be resubordinated to me several days from then, and I was very anxious to avoid a repetition of these occurrences so I had all the more cause to be concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P122.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to turn your attention to tab 31, please. You have before you, Admiral, a document which is dated 26th of October, 1991, and bears --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this document has been tendered already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Bears the signature or the endorsement of -- it says: "Commander of the Naval Sector," but Lieutenant General Pavle Strugar. Perhaps that is an error in the original title. You can assist us, if you wish, on whether or not the title of Strugar is correct there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- Your Honours, this document has not been tendered so far. We have not seen a document like this before. It doesn't bear a number, and it has not been tendered into evidence so far. I'm sure of that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This perhaps is my error. I thought it came in with an early ECMM witness. If that is the case, my apologies, but I thought it came in under an ECMM. It is my error. I'm terribly sorry. I have the wrong notation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel, also, for bringing that to my attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you if you are familiar with the content of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of what the purpose of the document was and how it was dealt with in the course of the campaign?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this document was to finally resolve, in a peaceful manner, the problem of the Dubrovnik crisis. There were supposed to be a normalisation of life within the town. There was a proposal that was sent to the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff comprising 11 points or items that had been formulated by the command of the 2nd Operational Group and approved, probably, by the superior command. There is an error in this document, the title itself. You can see that the Municipal Assembly of Dubrovnik I believe sent this document by telex, sent it back. I think the addressee is erroneous and also the signature says General Pavle Strugar, but the essence of this document is familiar to everyone. These are proposals that as of the 26th of October were very much in the focus of interest -- in the negotiations between the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff and the 2nd Operational Group. The main request put forward by this proposal was to hand over the weapons that had been amassed in the town of Dubrovnik itself and also for the volunteers and for the surplus men who had entered Dubrovnik after the 1st of October to leave town. This was actually the problem of demilitarisation of Dubrovnik; that was behind the request.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about some of the points in there, and I want to turn in particular your attention to point 7, where it says: "The JNA should guarantee that its members will respect the complete cease-fire and the safety of citizens and the city of Dubrovnik with its cultural and historical assets." Is this, in your view, a matter which is subject to condition or acceptance? In other words, should this be a point of bargaining, in your view, to protect citizens and cultural assets, or is it a mandate of law?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I believe this matter was worded inaccurately and erroneously, in part at least. There must be a guarantee of a complete cease-fire. I think that is a legitimate request and proposal. But certainly on the part of the citizens, the protection of cultural monuments is regulated by international conventions and this is something that cannot be negotiated in this way. I don't think that should have been included as part of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you agree that the safety of civilian citizens, of citizens, is also guaranteed by -- regulated by international law and -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is this proposal a document that you have heard referred to as an ultimatum? Have you heard that term used, "ultimatum"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Dubrovnik side called this document an ultimatum to surrender the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did the 2nd Operational Group genuinely expect the Croatian defenders to surrender their arms? Was there a general expectation that there would be compliance with the terms of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you take into account, Admiral, the events occurring elsewhere in Croatia, was it not expected that the Croatians would reject this document and the conditions therein?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation surrounding Dubrovnik was different from that faced by the other garrisons in Croatia. We had blocked the town from both sea and land. The town had not been demilitarised and it was armed but not nearly sufficiently armed to pose any real danger to the forces carrying out the blockade. We believed it was a well-founded belief, I believe, that the crisis could be resolved in a peaceful way. There had been certain indications that the proposal would be accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want to make sure you understand that my question surrounds the Croatians' willingness to disarm themselves in light of all that was happening in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you that in all the other garrisons and at the decision-making level of the Croatian state, no such proposal was ever accepted. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P123.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. Admiral, we are now going to ask to turn your attention to a map, Exhibit 20 -- I'm sorry, tab 22(A), and because time is very much a factor, we will try to move very swiftly through the next line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Everyone has his or her map in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, I would ask if you can assist us in what does this map -- what date is this map covering and what does it depict?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map covers the 14th of November, and it depicts the disposition of the forces of the 2nd Operational Group on that day in the Dubrovnik operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And at the top -- the centre and the top -- I'm sorry. In the centre and the top, what does it say? It says something "2OG." Above the date, just above the date.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Disposition group for -- the disposition of the forces for the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And does this map accurately depict the positions of the 2nd Operational Group on that date?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And is this map a working map, a map that the --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a working map of the staff, the headquarters of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. I'm going to try -- and yes, I'm sorry. The map was also -- indicates positions, and they were indicated contemporaneously with the making of the map? It is a contemporaneously-made -- a contemporaneous map?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. We're going to emphasise the area which is - let's see if I can help you try to focus on the map - which is around Dubrovnik itself and which is close to the Old Town of Dubrovnik. If you can indicate which units are in the area closest to the lines around Dubrovnik, which units of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The closest point to Dubrovnik that the units reached was that reached by the 472nd Brigade, more specifically its 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And are companies of the battalion indicated on this map, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. May I have the microphone closer, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, are you able to give us a scale on this map? I know it's not -- it doesn't appear to be written, but are you able to indicate a scale, if you can?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This scale is 1 against 100.000, I believe. The usual map that would be used by JNA units would be 1:100.000. That's what the scale would be, what I would expect it to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would that also have included the map you looked at yesterday for October?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would this map also -- well, were the positions from the 8th through the 13th of November different to the positions that are indicated on this map that represents the 14th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are. They are different.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And how so?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is that until the -- before the 14th of November there had been an operation carried out in the area of Dubrava, above Dubrovnik, and in the area of Komolac, just across Rijeka Dubrovacka, in the area where the 472nd Brigade was operating. The units of the 4th Battalion that were in the Zarkovica-Dubac area had been pulled out. I pulled that unit out, I detached it from the combat disposition, and in order to replace it, I set up a mixed TO detachment that operated for five days. The 3rd Battalion, too, had been introduced that had taken these fortifications above Dubrovnik, the fortifications of Bosanka, Gradci and Strincijera. You can see a disposition of the forces of the 3rd Battalion here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When was the 3rd Battalion introduced into this particular operation, combat operation you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was introduced on the 10th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: For the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd, can you please name the positions that are shown on the map as -- where it has 1, 2, 3 of the companies.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first company comprises the Bosanka area. The third company, the Strincijera Fort, and the fourth company, the Zarkovica area. The mortar battery occupies the Uskoplje area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, who was the commander for the period shown on this map and also from the 8th through the -- the 8th to the 13th, who was the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade -- sorry -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 25th of October, when the commander of the 3rd Battalion was seriously wounded, the Captain Kovacevic, Vladimir Kovacevic was the one who took over from the 25th of October, including this date the 14th of November, he was in command of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And particularly on the 10th of November when the 3rd Battalion was introduced into this combat operation, are you indicating that Vladimir Kovacevic was the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think the area is small enough that we're looking at, Mr. Usher, that we could try to put it on the ELMO. It might be easier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic, if you can take your pointer and place it on the position indicating the location of the 1st Company of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you move the map up a little bit, please. This lower portion is what we're looking at, if you could move it up. There. That's better. Thank you. And the focus is a little bit -- if it's possible to sharpen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, again, if you could please indicate the location with your pointer of the 1st Company of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd. And where is it located?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zarkovica - Dubac area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Could you speak --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zarkovica-Dubac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what weapons were in that location, Admiral, that could be in the range of the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That company, like any other, has mortars of 82 millimetres in addition to infantry arms. This kind of deployment is not identical to the deployment that took place later. There were some changes that were made in the combat deployment of the battalion later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The 2nd -- let me take a quick look and make sure I've covered -- The 2nd company, could you point it out, please, its location, and identify its location.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second company was in the area of Bosanka, the fortification of Bosanka. This is right across Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what type of weapons were within range of the Old Town that that company had at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, these mortars of 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were there any other weapons beside mortars that would have applied or belonged to either the company you just identified, the 2nd or the 1st --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There weren't any within those companies then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How about the entire battalion? Were there direct-fire weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The battalion had other weapons with which it supported these companies during attack, that is to say it had its artillery, plus the reinforcements it had got.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The 3rd company, could you please point it out and give its location.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd company was on the Strincijera fortress which, during the 10th -- the period between the 10th and the 12th, was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The other positions that are shown with weaponry, the 3rd company -- and what -- I'm sorry, Admiral, what is the marking where it says -- there is a triangle that says "3." Perhaps you can indicate what the marking around that is, it's a round circle with dots, black dots. It says "1" and "3." If you can bring your pointer down a little bit. A little lower. A bit lower yet. There you go.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are positions of the anti-armour company of the battalion, however the number is not there. This is the 4th company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what type of weapons are you referring to when you say "anti-armour"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This company had 82-millimetre mortars, it had recoilless guns, it had launchers for rockets, Maljutkas, and it also had anti-aircraft guns, 20-millimetre ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were the weapons you have just described of the 3rd Battalion within reach or range of the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this position, this anti--armour company, on this particular position was not within reach -- or rather, the Old Town was not within reach or range yet. All its firearms were deployed in order to be able to target the Old Town. It's not depicted on this map, but it was only later that it took these positions on Zarkovica from which targets in the Old Town could be engaged. However, as regards artillery -- or rather, mortars, 120-millimetre mortars that were here within this circle, that was the artillery of the 3rd Battalion in the area of Uskoplje. From there, the Old Town could be targeted, including the city harbour and part of the new town of Dubrovnik outside the old walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, can you indicate where the units of the 3rd Battalion were between the 10th of November and the 13th of November.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 10th and the 13th, they were in attack. This battalion was introduced on the 10th for combat operations. The task was to take over the fort of Gradci, Dubrava, and Fort Strincijera. And before that, before the 10th of November it was resting in the Ivanica/Trebinje area because it was taken out after the losses it had sustained on the 23rd and 24th of October. An order was given to withdraw them and to give them a period of rest of about ten days. I mean, it was not within my troops, but I know what they did when they were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The units of the 3rd Battalion were within firing range of the Old Town of Dubrovnik during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who had ordered the 3rd Battalion to take these positions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Operational Group gave orders regarding the main part of the task of this operation. The details were given by the command of the sector, the details regarding the 3rd Battalion and how these forts should be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there a degree of risk in having this type of weaponry so close to the city?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. Such potential danger did exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can we take a look, Admiral, at some of the other positions very quickly that are on this map. I want to ask you about the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade. Was it at that point under the command of the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th Naval Military Sector, yes. This battalion was on leave in Podgorica until the 5th of November. On the 5th of November, they came to their area; it can be seen here, opposite Rijeka Dubrovacka. Its deployment can be seen above Mokosica above the settlement of Mokosica, Podbrijezje, Petrovo Selo, et cetera; that's the area. It was supposed to take over -- or rather, to enter the combat deployment of the 2nd Battalion of the Trebinje Brigade. It did take over from them, as was ordered previously; namely, that on the 6th of November the entire brigade withdraw from that area and go north-west. This battalion came in good time, carried out the necessary preparations, and took over the duties involved in that combat deployment, as can be seen on this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic, were -- what -- were the weapons of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade within range of the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On that date. Admiral, can I ask, please, when was Bosanka taken? What date? 19 A. Bosanka was taken on the 10th, between the 8th and 10th of November,in that 20 period of time. I'm sorry. I beg your pardon. You asked about the 5th -- or 21 rather, the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade? Was that the previous question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was within range?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It was, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, then it’s all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. What was your -- and your answer was for that date?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Its artillery pieces were not within reach or range of the Old Town. They were on the other side of Rijeka Dubrovacka.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can take a look at some of the surrounding units very quickly, if you can identify what they were, starting at the -- it says "the 5th of the 3rd lpbr," just what the unit was, its location, and what weapons it had. Do you see it on the left? It says "the 5th of the 3rd" -- yes. Describe the unit, its location, and the weaponry it had. Or at least the location.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area of Zaton. This is where the companies of the 3rd Light Brigade were deployed. This was a unit, a newly established unit, poorly armed, and for the most part it was used for auxiliary routes, for controlling territory, and for giving assistance to others. It was poorly armed and insufficiently trained. These are its companies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And then moving along very quickly, the one -- it says "1, 3 at pmtb." A little bit over to your left -- left, more, more, please. There you go.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. What is that unit and where is it located?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the 1st Battalion -- or rather, the 1st Company of -- there seems to be a mistake here. This is a company of the battalion. This is a mistake. There is no such unit here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Then the 3rd of the -- it says: "3 of the 5th pmtbr" -- I'm sorry, I beg your pardon. You're having to repeat yourself unintentionally. It It says: "3 pmtb," below, if you move down a little bit. It says 3 --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what is the unit? Where is it located, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say. I know all the designations and I think I know everything from the combat rules, but now is this a mistake or perhaps it's a territorial battalion. But I don't know this particular designation, "pmt."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, from what you're describing in terms of range of weaponry, what was the -- which units that -- during this time period on that day, or let's say between the 8th and the 13th of November, were within range -- had weapons that were within range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that period, between the 8th and the 13th of November, the units that can be seen here across Rijeka Dubrovacka, that is to say the 1st Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, and the 2nd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, which are the main units in this combat deployment, due to the configuration of the terrain and the tasks that they got, and as it can be seen from the combat deployment, their companies could not have targeted the Old Town, because its mortars were behind in terms of the combat deployment, that is to say outside effective reach of the Old Town in terms of distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Then which units had reach of the Old Town, firing reach of the Old Town? I'm sorry, range.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, which was brought into action on the 10th of November, and on the 14th of November, after having taken these forts which we can see here, it came into this kind of combat deployment in terms of its companies and artillery support. From these positions, it could have targeted -- well, not exactly within effective range if its objective was to engage targets in the Old Town, but it could have targeted the Old Town, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, there are some units on the outer edges of this area of the map - you may have to move your map over a little bit to see it - and I just want to quickly ask you about those. To the right, somewhat below Trebinje, there's a circle, a black circle, that says -- can you move it a bit more. Thanks. This is good. Right. I can't read the abbreviation very clearly, but if you could tell us what it is and what the "130 mm" designation signifies.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is actually a division, a mobile division, coastal artillery division, 130 millimetres. These are cannons for supporting the units of the 472nd Brigade. Their effective range is about 15 to 16 kilometres. That is why its positions are in this area of Volujac, near Trebinje. That's why they're so far away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do they have firing range of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Their range covered the entire area of Dubrovnik as a town in view of the fact that they had quite a long-range.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And above it says -- there's a 472nd designation with a black circle. Yes, please, could you describe that position and the weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a Howitzer division, 105 millimetres, Howitzers of 105 millimetres, and their range was about 10 kilometres. They were intended to be support to the battalions to the right of Dubrovnik. Dubrovnik and the Old Town were at the end of effective range, so I believe they could not have been used except in great necessity. They could have targeted Rijeka Dubrovacka, though, in this area here. The 472nd Brigade, this is the command post of the brigade in this area of Cerovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, the units that you have identified that were within firing range -- that had weapons that were within firing range of the Old Town in the period 8th through 13th of November, to what formations did those units belong?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They belonged to the 9th Sector, or rather, the 2nd Operational Group at a higher level. That is to say that at that time the brigade, since it had not been taken out as was ordered in the previous orders of the 6th of November, it still remained within combat deployment and it remained subordinated to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And as part -- did you indicate as part of the 2nd Operational Group as the overall formation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you can take a quick look at the coastal waters. Can you indicate, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think you'll have to move your map up a little bit, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What are -- where are vessels of the -- of your sector indicated. We have blue and red markings. Can you say which are the red?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue are my ships, the patrol boats. And here in front of Dubrovnik there is the number 2. There are two ships PC and one in the Mljet canal and one in the Zupa channel. This symbolically shows their tasks, providing security in the channels, for the bays, within the blockade of Dubrovnik and the harbours, the ports, near Dubrovnik. The colour blue denotes communications and the routes that speedboats and other fast boats took from Ston, Metkovic, Opuzen, used to supply the town with weapons. So this route of theirs across the islands was supposed to be intercepted, hence the patrolling of these speedboats.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, what do the red markings signify on the waters? There are five red markings. Do you see them? What do they signify?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those are patrol boats in their positions -- or rather, within a blockade line, or rather, patrol line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Perhaps it's been a little less than clear. Those patrol boats belong to which forces?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are patrol boats of the 16th Border Naval Unit, and they are subordinated to the 9th Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And just to clarify, the blue -- well, figures, or however we want to call them, the blue elliptical or triangular figures that you have running along the coast, would you again please clarify what those represent. Those blue figures; do you see them? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They represent speedboats or other fast boats of the Dubrovnik defence that took these routes and used these islands for smuggling, for bringing in contraband weapons and personnel for the defence of the town of Dubrovnik from this area Metkovic, Ston, Opuzen. They usually did this during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask at this time to move this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P124.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, between 8 and 14 November, were there any changes in the subordination relationships of the 2nd -- of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade? Was there any change in the subordination relationships of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 10th of November, the 3rd Battalion was introduced that had been on leave. It was brought into the battle to take the forts that we spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you indicate from the 10th of November whether or not the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd became directly subordinated to the 9th Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you explain the difference between direct and indirect fire.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Direct fire is fire used to hit the target directly, the target that can be seen from the firing positions where the weapons are positioned, the weapons used for firing. Indirect firing is when you can't see the target from the firing positions, but rather from an observation post. The hits are being reported, and there's a correction of firing. There's an observation post, and then the observation post reports back to whoever's firing on the success of firing, whether the target has been hit or not. And then this is reported to the commander who is next to the weapon. There is the crew, the firing crew, which is located at the firing position.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. I want to take one second; I want to just check a note. Thank you. Which positions would have allowed the best use of direct-fire weapons during the period of combat operations you have just discussed, in November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in relation to targeting the town of Dubrovnik or generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You're right. Excuse me. I'll rephrase the question. Which positions would have provided the -- would have allowed the best use of direct-fire weapons toward the Old Town of Dubrovnik during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the map, it is clear that in the Zarkovica area there's an elevation about 350 metres high. And from there, a clear unobstructed view opens on to the Old Town. As for the other positions, Bosanka and Strincijera, there's a rock just in front, the rock of Srdj, which obstructs the view. As for the use of artillery, the mortars, 120-millimetre mortars and far-range cannon, you would need observation posts placed at certain elevations; Zarkovica, if possible. They would observe the hits and then report back to the firing commander. At Zarkovica, there should be an observation post, and the short-range weapons firing positions, too, which can be used to target certain points inside the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say "the town," are you referring to the Old Town, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Old Town, but I'm referring to the town of Dubrovnik as a whole, because most of the artillery had been positioned outside the Old Town. And in order to neutralise those, these weapons were being used, at least pursuant to all the orders that we had issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral. If I can ask you, please, to turn your attention to tab 23. Admiral, this is an order dated the 5th of November, 1991, addressed to the 2nd Operational Group command, the 472nd Motorised Brigade, and the 9th VPS for the units marked. Can you please indicate, whose order is this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was produced by my command; it bears my signature. And the time, or rather, the date given is the 5th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what -- can you give us a brief indication of the significance of this order for the operations upcoming.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crux of this order, pursuant to the tasks given to the sector by the 2nd Operational Group, I was supposed to set up a mixed detachment that would replace the 4th Battalion of the Trebinje Brigade. Previously -- I must add, previously I was supposed to draft a statement and send it to Admiral Brovet because of firing, acts of provocation that were directed at some hotels in town but outside the Old Town. It was not proven exactly who was to blame, but probably the blame was on both sides, the Croatian side and our side equally. In order to reduce the possibility of using artillery fire against the town, I removed the 4th Battalion of the Trebinje Brigade and replaced it with the Territorial Defence mixed detachment, who did not have the same strong artillery. They did not have 120-millimetre mortars, but rather, short-range mortars. As for the guns, 40 and 60 millimetre that were supposed to be used for anti-aircraft defence, those were not used from the area to target the town. Therefore, I believe that the problem of these acts of provocation and firing on the town was thereby eliminated or dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the section under -- it says "point 2" of this order, there's a reference to the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. Would you please indicate what is discussed about that brigade there.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here it says that the battalion is assembled in the area of deployment and that it should remain until further notice in the Talez area. It had been pulled out from combat, therefore it is outside the zone of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So by going into Talez, is it making it available for use in operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was on leave, resting, on the 5th, when this was --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did it leave its position from Talez and become available for combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This battalion was brought before it was introduced. I think it was between the 8th and the 10th of November, but I can't specify the date. I don't have that document now, but it must have been between the 8th and the 10th because it was introduced on the 10th, so give or take a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask to move this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P125.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, were -- what was the number of combat casualties in the course of this attack, and which units sustained them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During these operations, there were heavy losses, especially when Bosanka was taken. This mixed TO detachment, which did not have any powerful artillery, there was a limited operation with no use of artillery, especially not against the town itself. I think they had four dead and many wounded. When those dead and wounded were being evacuated, there were new losses that were sustained because the area was clear, the whole rock was exposed, and the Croatian artillery from the town itself opened fire, which made it impossible for them to evacuate their dead and wounded, not even at night. This lasted for about two or three days, the evacuation itself took about two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was that the total number of casualties for that operation? What about from the 10th?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th, when the 3rd Battalion was brought in, and during the fighting -- the fighting around the forts, the three forts, they did have several men who were killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And were those men casualties of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who issued the orders for this operation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And I'd ask you, please, to turn to tab 24. Admiral, do you recognise this document which bears the date of 10 November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a combat order that was produced by my command on the 10th of November, and it bears my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. And was this order issued following or pursuant to any other orders of a superior command? What was the purpose of the order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order that was written on the 10th, and it pertains to an operation that was supposed to be carried out on the 11th of November. It sets out the tasks for my subordinate units, and it was written pursuant to a decision on operations by the command of the 2nd Operational Group, which ran the entire operation in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The reference on the first page in the first paragraph to the general access of Bosanka, which units were to have participated in the extension of the attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 472nd Brigade, the 3rd Light Brigade, and the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. In order to better understand the situation, we must point out the following: The 3rd Battalion was operating along a special route. It would only take the rock just above Dubrovnik, and that's why special emphasis is given to their tasks. The remaining forces were active in Rijeka Dubrovacka, the 3rd Light Brigade, and the 1st and 2nd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, and that's why these tasks were separate tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say "the rock just above Dubrovnik," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the Bosanka, Strincijera, and Gradci forts. These were the forts that were taken in this attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask to move this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P126.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you please turn your attention to tab 25. Admiral, before you is a document dated 10 November, 1991, and it bears the signature of an individual named Radovan Klikovac. Who is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an officer who was in charge of the organisation and mobilisation at the command of the 9th Sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And it is addressed to whom?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is addressed to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. And it was probably produced pursuant to a request to forward information on officers and soldiers who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd ask to move this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P127.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tab 26, please. I want to ask you very quickly about this document, Admiral. It is a combat order. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a combat order produced by my command dated the 12th of November. It bears my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And does this order confirm that the 9th VPS is, in fact, issuing orders to the 472nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd ask to move this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The next -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P128.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you can please turn your attention to tab 27. Just briefly taking a look at a document dated 13 November, 1991, Admiral, do you recognise this order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was produced by my command on the 13th of November, and it bears my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And in this document, does it indicate that you are -- that your command is now issuing orders to the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document comprises three units, the 3rd Battalion and the 16th Border Naval Detachment, the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Both this order and the order we just looked at from -- excuse me, from the 11th -- I'm sorry, from the 12th and the 13th of November, are issued in the midst of combat operations, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask to move this last document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P129.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic, was the Old Town of Dubrovnik shelled in the course of the combat operations we have just discussed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must point out briefly that during the operation itself between the 10th and the 12th, personally I was not aware of any shelling of the Old Town. When the operations began, I was with the 3rd Light Brigade. My chief of staff was back at the command post, and Captain -- Colonel Kovacevic was with the 3rd Battalion. Finally, on the 10th or on the 11th, I believe, at the command post awaiting further action, based on information that I had received about the Old Town being shelled from the chief of staff of the brigade who had gone to Kupari for reporting, I asked whether and why they had shelled the Old Town. He told me that they didn't shell the Old Town. I called the chief of staff to confirm whether he had seen him in command of the guns and what was being targeted. He said that the 76-millimetre guns were being trained on Srdj, but that they were not targeting the town. I told him this was only an excuse, and that even if they weren't targeting the town, every shell that missed its target, every single volley that missed its target, would fly past Srdj and land on the Old Town. Whether he was doing it in order to take revenge on his former commander, brigade commander, who had fled to Dubrovnik and organised the town's defence, or whether he was doing this deliberately pursuant to someone else's orders, why --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, sorry to cut you off. Was the Old Town of Dubrovnik -- did you come to learn that the Old Town of Dubrovnik was shelled during the combat operations in this period? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you make an inquiry into the shelling of the Old Town during this period of time, an inquiry or an investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following this operation, I conducted an investigation. I questioned the commanders and officers who may have been responsible for these operations, the chief of staff of the 472nd Brigade, Major Komar, his commander, Colonel Obrad Vicic. I also called the battalion commander following the completion of this operation from the command post when he arrived in Kupari. I talked to him. I discussed with him who had done this, whether it was his units, the artillery of the 472nd Brigade, or a different battalion. He insisted that it had not been him. I asked to have the chief of staff removed as well as the brigade commander, to have them both resign. And that's what I did about this investigation, but no further inquiries were made.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you inquire whether or not there was any outgoing fire from the Old Town, or was it told to you? Did you inquire?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During those interviews, the commander of the 3rd Battalion insisted that he had been under permanent fire from the ramparts and from the turrets of the Old Town and that there must have been mortars, either in the Old Town itself or just next to the ramparts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there any outgoing fire from the Old Town, Admiral? What is your assessment? Was there any outgoing fire from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my assessment, even if there had been any such fire, it could only have been an act of provocation by 120-millimetre gun or something like that. But certainly there could have been no fire coming from the Old Town that would have posed a real threat to our units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which units of the units under your command shelled the Old Town between the 10th and 13th, and with what weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade was in a position from which this could have been done. Possibly the artillery of the 472nd Brigade also took part, its 130-millimetre guns, but I have no evidence that those were ever used.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade at this time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did he control the situation at all times during these operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you order the shelling of the Old Town during the November operations, Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you personally observe the attack on the Old Town, Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't personally witness this. I was in no position to see that from the position in which I was at the time. However, based on the reports that I received after the operation, this was possible -- it was possible to ascertain that. I did, in fact, ascertain that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you did not order this operation, how could the shelling of the Old Town, in light of the previous orders prohibiting the shelling of the Old Town, have occurred in the course of a well-planned combat operation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assessment at the time was - and it has only been reinforced by further questioning - that this was a willful attack by the battalion commander receiving support and in coordination, in combat coordination, with the chief of staff of the brigade, Major Komar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you become aware of civilian casualties and damage to civilian objects that resulted from this shelling or these shellings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During the entire operation, we were not aware of any civilian casualties or of the extent of destruction, except on the 6th of December when we expected that, but not this time around.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was the shelling of the Old Town that you've just discussed during the time period of 10 - 13 November, was it ever investigated within the 2nd Operational Group or by the command of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was Strugar -- General Strugar, excuse me, informed of the investigation that you had begun?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After questioning Major Komar about his role in terms of support to the 3rd Battalion and the targeting of the Old Town, on the 10th or possibly on the 11th, I informed the chief of staff. I'm not sure if it was General Damjanovic, but I think it was him, or possibly Stankovic. I requested the resignation of the chief of staff and the brigade commander because of those activities. The commander of the brigade group was not at his -- of the operational group was not at his command post. I'm not sure where he was at the time. We discussed the extent of damage, and he told me that he would inform the commander about this, because he did not have the authority to deal with this issue. The next day, I asked to speak to General Kandic and General Strugar yet again to have these officers replaced by other officers, and I failed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You failed in having them replaced or you failed in speaking to them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did speak to them, but the command of the 2nd Operational Group, or rather, General Strugar did not have any competent officers to offer as replacements. The general told me that he would send an officer who was the commander of an armoured unit, but that he would only send this officer later. Therefore, the situation remained unresolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the transcript I believe contains an error. On page 31, line 19, it says "General Kandic" whereas it should read "Admiral Kandic." And the next thing is, this last answer at line 25, it reads: "The general told me," and what the admiral actually said is that the admiral would send another competent officer and the way I heard it was a reference to Admiral Kandic. Therefore, I would like to have this clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you seek to clarify the position, please, Ms. Somers. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you said, Admiral Jokic, in the transcript -- let's see -- that someone of the two persons, Kandic or Strugar, would send an officer who was a commander of an armoured unit, to whom were you referring? Who would send it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Admiral Kandic was the one who said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were the two officers you referred to, Captain Kovacevic and Komar, chief of staff, ever replaced? Excuse me. I beg your pardon. The brigade -- I beg your pardon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought it was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, I have a wrong note.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were the brigade commander and chief of staff Komar ever removed or replaced in connection with these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And was Captain Kovacevic removed or replaced in connection with these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be a convenient time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the morning -- first morning break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic, based on your findings and your recommendation to replace the chief of staff Komar and the brigade commander Vicic, what measures did you propose to take against Captain Kovacevic, whose conduct - that is the shelling of the Old Town - you deemed to have been willfully done?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not ask for his removal or replacement. I was not convinced that it was his fault, in view of the fact that an investigation had not been carried out and that around Dubrovnik there were other units belonging to the brigade as well as the brigade artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your finding of his willfully shelling did not lead you to take any action against him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I thought that it was the responsibility of the brigade command, and he was part of that brigade. I did not learn anything then, but only later that he was the main perpetrator and that the others just supported his actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there any other reason you did not further pursue an investigation into Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now I do not remember that very clearly, but I think that he was given certain support and that perhaps that was the reason then why I did not raise the issue of his replacement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Support by whom?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the support of individuals from the command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which individuals?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the chief of staff and the commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you believe he had the support of -- by "the commander of the 2nd Operational Group," to whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to General Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you discuss your findings about Captain Kovacevic's actions with General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time I did not succeed in talking to him, because he was not at the command post. Due to his obligations, he was often absent, either in other corps or in Podgorica or reporting in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you shortly thereafter discuss your findings, if not immediately?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we talked about that once when he was in Kupari, but the conversation boiled down to the following, that we did not know whether certain damage was greater, and that's where it all remained. Actually, can I just say something very briefly? We thought -- or rather, in the commands, we thought that the other side was exaggerating the damage, that they were not presenting the entire truth. Their newspapers wrote that all of Dubrovnik was ablaze, that they had a lot of ruins and casualties. So we, as units were in between, so to speak, we did not know what the actual state of affairs was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you do anything to determine what the actual state of affairs was at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you agree that irrespective of the degree of damage to the Old Town, the fact of shelling of the Old Town was prohibited and that was known to all persons in the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that the shelling, irrespective of damage, the shelling of a protected place that is a subject of orders prohibiting that shelling is a serious violation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that you had proposed the removal of the chief of staff of the brigade and the brigade commander. What was General Strugar's response to that, if any?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that at that time I did not find him; he was absent. But I think I talked to the chief of staff. He told me - and I heard later as well - they did not have such officers, that their officers ranked from lieutenant colonel upwards, and that he could not supply me with appropriate officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who had the authority to remove or replace officers of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the commander of the 2nd Operational Group had that authority. I had authority over the units that were subordinated to me, like the 3rd Battalion and the brigade. However, since these were units that were temporarily subordinated, I had to seek approval from my superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you had recommended the removal and replacement of these officers for what you perceived to have been wrongdoing or indiscipline, what would you have expected General Strugar to have done, as the most senior officer in the area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to call them and to replace them -- or rather, to find appropriate officers who could replace them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you could please turn to your tabs -- to tab 28. Admiral, are you -- were there protests by international community representatives or the Croatians concerning the shelling of the Old Town and of the city as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document refers to the protest of the international monitoring mission on the 10th of November. Of the chief of mission, Mr. Van Houten, and his protest addressed to General Kadijevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And also delivered to whom? Whose names are indicated above the phrase "international monitoring mission"? To whom was this letter delivered?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letter was delivered to General Raseta, who was negotiating with the Croatian government in Zagreb, and General Strugar, commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say General Raseta negotiating for the government, was he a negotiator for the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the JNA negotiator in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask you about the text of this document. "To General Kadijevic, Minister of Defence, breach of cease-fire in Dubrovnik. I have been informed by the monitoring mission team of the European community in Dubrovnik that the shelling of the city is not only continuing but that it is intensive. The monitors have noticed actions in the area of the Old City walls. General Raseta, the deputy commander of the 5th military district, was informed about this breach of cease-fire, as was General Strugar, the commander of the federal forces of the region of Dubrovnik, and as such without any reply. I am now forwarding this information to you in the interests of security for the monitors of the European community in Dubrovnik. Their lives are at stake due to the actions of the Yugoslav People's Army. I plead that you order a cease-fire immediately so that the monitoring teams in the Dubrovnik port can go through a safe evacuation." Then it indicates that it has been delivered, et cetera, et cetera, signed, "Chief of Mission, D. J. Van Houten." Was there any response by General Strugar to this letter?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any. I don't have any knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did General Strugar call together the officers of his subordinate units and indicate that this letter had come to his attention and pass it on to these officers to be passed down to subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Rodic please be asked to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your microphone, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. It would be logical to ask before this question whether the witness knows of General Strugar having received this letter at all. And then once this question had been put, it is only then on the basis of the answer given that further questions can be put as to whether he did anything about it, et cetera. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I do notice the content of the letter suggests that the matter was directly put to General Strugar before this written letter. But I think you're alerted to the issue, Ms. Somers. You could resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Perhaps I can just ask whether or not you or any of the other officers, to your knowledge, heard of the contents of this letter in any means or manner while in the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have heard of the contents, or rather, elements of the contents. But I don't think I had this letter. General Strugar had to ask me whether these were my units or what the problem was, or rather, how he resolved the response to this letter. I know that things could have gone beyond me, because we did have a negotiating team that talked to Dubrovnik and the mission then. So perhaps it went along those channels, that is to say not including me. I believe I was asked, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document in evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P130.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you please turn your attention to tab 29. In front of you, Admiral, is a document indicating a delivery date of 11 November, signed by or bearing the endorsement of chief of staff Colonel Dr. Vuk Obradovic to Ambassador Van Houten, the chief of the international monitoring mission in Zagreb. It reads -- please indicate, if you know, who a Colonel Dr. Vuk Obradovic is.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Obradovic was chef de cabinet to the federal secretary, General Kadijevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: "Your Excellency, Regarding your letter dated 10 November, 1991, and by the order of army General Veljko Kadijevic, the Federal Secretary for National Defence, I would like to inform you there was truly an intensified shelling of the Dubrovnik region with focus on the region of Bosanka and Srdja, and this is due to the fact that there were strengthened provocations and attacks from the Croatian Armed forces upon the JNA. "At the same time, I would like to once again bring to your attention upon the fact -- I'm sorry -- to bring your attention upon the fact that the Croatian Armed Forces have been opened fire from the direction of Stari Grad (Old City), and even with that the JNA units did not act against the old city centre of Dubrovnik, as can also be seen from your letter. "Even though the JNA does nothing to endanger the lives of your monitors, we are ready to enable a safe evacuation for them, if you so regulate. For the cease-fire to take effect, it should also be acted upon the Croatian Armed forces to cease with the attacks upon the JNA, given that our side is at cease-fire, and that the JNA forces only answer to the open fire once the lives of their members are at stake. I ask you to arrange the particulars of the agreement with General Major Andreja Raseta." Signed. Is there a denial in this letter of shelling of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Considering your previous testimony about the events of the November shelling of the Old Town, would you conclude that the representations or the contents about the Old Town contained in this letter are false, are not true?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have to be very specific. I claimed that the Old Town had been shelled and that I learned about this after the action had been completed, but that was between the 10th and 12th November, when the 3rd Battalion of the brigade had been introduced. That is to say between the 10th and 12th. Up to the 10th of November, in the period when Bosanka was being taken, the fort of Bosanka, there were operations around the Old Town, or rather, Srdj and other old forts were targeted. However, it was not established then by way of fact that the Old Town was targeted at that time. That is what I wish to say in order to be as precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you agree, Admiral, however, that what is said, that is that "the JNA units did not act against the old city centre of Dubrovnik," is it incorrect? Is it incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for this period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I ask to move this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecution Exhibit P131.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How do you view, Admiral, the reaction of a command of the 2nd Operational Group to the November shelling of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that at the level of my sector and particularly at the level of the command of the 2nd Operational Group, it was necessary to carry out an investigation and establish exactly what had been going on in terms of what the units were doing around Dubrovnik, especially the 472nd Brigade and its 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what is your assessment, what are your views, about the lack of measures taken to undertake such investigation and to establish exactly what happened? Again, I address it to the lack of action by the command of the 2nd Operational Group, your views on that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that an investigation was supposed to have been carried out at the level of my command or at the level of the 2nd Operational Group, because the brigade was under its command all the time. It was only temporarily assigned to me for being used over a certain period of time. That is to say that I was supposed to have been ordered to carry out an investigation or the investigation should have been carried out by the organs of the 2nd Operational Group, within their own organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you, under the circumstances, view -- feel that the command of the 2nd Operational Group fell short of its responsibility to investigate and deal with this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can be the judge of my superior command now, then it can be put that way. However --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be allowed to finish his answer. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... accidental, Mr. Petrovic. The two commenced to speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. It was my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Admiral. You were saying, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is what I wished to say: I think differently now, and of course at that time my thinking was incomplete and different in relation to what I think now. This is what I'm trying to say. I don't know what the command of the 2nd Operational Group bore in mind, what guided them, and why such a decision was made not to carry out an investigation. Because the command had other information, too, as to what was going on beyond our lines. It had a negotiating team which was in daily negotiations with the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik, and they also had other intelligence, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Admiral. Moving on. I'd like to ask you to look to tab 30, which is a map. Admiral Jokic, do you recognise this particular map?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a map of the deployment of the units of the 2nd Operational Group for the 2nd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is the scale of this map, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The scale is 1:50.000. It's a larger scale than the one used in the previous map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, would this map also reflect the deployment of units on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the deployment that applied on the 6th of December also. Practically, it didn't change, this disposition, this deployment, since the 14th of November, the 2nd of December, and the 6th of December. The deployment remained the same. The units in the immediate vicinity of Dubrovnik were not moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, Admiral, the upper left-hand corner of your map, what type of map does this indicate this is and what situation does it cover?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the deployment of the forces of the 2nd Operational Group, a grouping of units in the blockade of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I understand. And in the upper left-hand corner, what type of map is it called? In the left, can you see, Admiral, yes --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a working map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this map a contemporaneous map, in other words one that was used at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This completely reflects the situation on the 2nd of December. You can see on this map the 3rd Battalion stayed in the same positions, bearing in mind the fact that on the 13th of November there had been a cease-fire, a truce, therefore the positions of these units did not change. But the 472nd Brigade had been pulled out, and you can see the position of that brigade here on the map. It was in the area of the 2nd Corps. But its 3rd Battalion remained in its previous position.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, let's -- if it's -- if you can do it comfortably, can you indicate, by the 6th of December, what territory was controlled by the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This may be convenient, Mr. Usher, to put on the ELMO. I think the area would lend itself to being discussed that way. Let me just take a look at the size -- in just a few minutes. I think we'll start big and we'll work our way down. I think it's a bit tough.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Admiral, what territory was held by the 2nd Operational Group as of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
